reviews.license: MIT OR Apache-2.0; package declaration; prefer MIT where applicable
reviews.reuse: First whole-crate import candidate; adapt its job plans to the existing redb/Wasmi service.
reviews.findings: Existing limits cover YAML bytes/depth/nodes/aliases, matrix combinations and run jobs. Deadline::after stores Instant::checked_add as Option; overflow therefore becomes no deadline. Secret redacts Debug but deliberately serializes plaintext.
reviews.adaptations: Reject overflowing or absent deadlines at untrusted boundaries; freeze event/revision/policy inputs. Store secret handles, not serialized runner credentials. Do not treat the runner protocol as authenticated Gitr worker authority.
reviews.acceptance: Lustr differential fixtures for expressions, aliases, matrices, cron, cancellation and duplicate events; deadline overflow regression; no plaintext secrets in durable plans/logs; expired-worker fencing and atomic result publication.

reviews.reuse: Reuse whole expression/model crates and test corpus; run the auditor as a build-time tool or adapt selected policies.
reviews.findings: Maintained expression/model crates are inside the current monorepo, not the old standalone repositories. The sampled expression API preserves source spans and distinguishes contexts from dataflow contexts; parsing has an explicit depth error.
reviews.adaptations: Keep Rbit as the planner unless parity tests justify consolidation. Security analysis is not an authorization proof or an execution sandbox. Audit rules which require network lookups and the full CLI parser/native dependency closure.
reviews.acceptance: Hostile PR title/body interpolation, token permissions, unpinned uses, fork-event secrets, poisoned caches and deep-expression fixtures; run offline-capable checks without ambient GitHub credentials.

reviews.license: Apache-2.0; root license header and package declaration inspected
reviews.reuse: Substantial package-family pilot for chunk-aware large assets, not wholesale replacement by git-xet.
reviews.findings: Current workspace consolidates packages into xet-data/client/core-structures/runtime. The root lists git2 and another redb version; the data crate exposes telemetry and depends on the Xet client. The sampled exports are not an algorithm audit.
reviews.adaptations: No libgit2 or automatic cloud/telemetry dependency in Gitr core. Select a lawful Apache-compatible build composition first; align dependencies, preserve Git LFS SHA-256 identities and retain ordinary GitHub whole-object transfers. A Xet client is not a self-hosted CAS server.
reviews.acceptance: Authorized disposable CAS roundtrip, corrupt reconstruction rejection, cancellation/resume, bounded memory and cache quotas; measure compressed Unreal/Unity assets, patch insertions, network bytes and physical writes against the current FastCDC/LFS path.

reviews.license: MIT alternative inspected; preserve upstream notices
reviews.reuse: Whole query-library family is an optional graph-query candidate over redb, not a replacement database. Keep GitQL as the first general query pilot.
reviews.findings: QueryableDataset abstracts internal terms, pattern lookups and graph enumeration; spareval has no direct Oxigraph store dependency. Default graph enumeration collects a HashSet and graph unions deduplicate in memory.
reviews.adaptations: Implement a repository/revision-scoped dataset with indexed redb lookups. Override expensive defaults; enforce intermediate-work/memory limits, not only LIMIT. Deny network SERVICE and mutation interfaces unless explicitly authorized. Preserve raw Git path identity when mapping terms.
reviews.acceptance: Cross-repository isolation, graph-name enumeration, cyclic/path queries, duplicates, cancellation, large joins and cold-start/RSS tests; validate query semantics before introducing a second query language.

reviews.license: MIT alternative inspected; preserve upstream notices
reviews.reuse: Whole incremental-computation library pilot for derived code analysis; do not replace redb authority.
reviews.findings: Inputs and pure query functions support memoized recomputation. The inspected manifest also has an optional persistence feature and interlocks macro versions; persistence must not be mistaken for consensus or a stable Gitr data format.
reviews.adaptations: Explicit commit/blob/parser/model/config keys; deterministic pure queries, cancellation and bounded caches. Treat any persisted memoization as regenerable and versioned independently from durable forge/jobs.
reviews.acceptance: Rename/delete/branch-switch invalidation, parser/model upgrades, cold restore and concurrent readers; compare recomputation count and peak memory with current blob-keyed reuse.

reviews.license: MIT; selected source header inspected; full distribution closure pending
components: diskann graph algorithms and provider contracts
reviews.reuse: Whole Rust ANN library with a Gitr redb-derived provider is preferable to writing an ANN implementation from scratch.
reviews.findings: Current DataProvider supports external/internal ID mapping, per-operation context and failure guards; Delete distinguishes soft deletion from release. These are concrete host-storage contracts, not only a standalone vector server.
reviews.adaptations: Version immutable index generations with embedding/model identity; do not expose recycled internal IDs as Git identities. Keep ANN adjacency separate from code/ref authority. Preserve exact lexical fallback and authorize the candidate set before returning results.
reviews.acceptance: Recall against exact search, filtered recall, deletion/ID-reuse races, interrupted inserts/rebuilds, snapshot consistency and p50/p95/RSS/write-amplification measurements on Gitr corpora.

reviews.license: MIT declared in README and workspace header; transitive ancestry review pending
components: older Rust DiskANN derivative and disk-query implementation
reviews.reuse: Keep as a comparative fork, not the default solely because its README calls Microsoft a partial Rust port.
reviews.findings: README identifies ancestry from Microsoft DiskANN/rust and NSG. Its workspace comments out the build_disk_index driver. Neither this observation nor its completeness claim proves disk-query behavior. Current Microsoft source already supplies a Rust provider API.
reviews.adaptations: Establish exact shared history and per-file provenance before transplantation; compare current implementations and dependency closures, not historical project descriptions. Do not infer a tested pure-Rust or complete implementation from README text.
reviews.acceptance: Compile both pins with Lustr, run equivalent memory/disk/query/delete tests and compare corrupt-input behavior and recall; identify any unique tested algorithm improvement before carrying a fork delta.

reviews.license: MIT declared in selected moon_affected package; full closure pending
reviews.reuse: Import a coherent task-planning family or adapt a focused subset; it is not an isolated drop-in equivalent to rbit-workflow.
reviews.findings: moon_affected has many local workspace dependencies. TaskTracker reads GlobalEnvBag and filesystem contents; a deleted content-filtered input currently takes the nonexistent-file path. Whole workspace features also include process execution, Extism and native TLS options.
reviews.adaptations: Feed immutable before/after snapshots and captured environment descriptors rather than live worktrees. Treat deletions conservatively. Use redb durable plans/claims, not an additional job authority; toolchain plugins are not automatically Wasmi-compatible.
reviews.acceptance: Deleted/renamed inputs, inherited configuration, environment changes, false-negative affected-task selection, deterministic cache keys, archive traversal/symlink poisoning and interrupted cache publication.

reviews.license: MIT OR Apache-2.0; package declaration; prefer MIT where applicable
reviews.reuse: Whole-library candidate for byte/text patching and three-way file merge; compare with existing Gitoxide facilities before adding redundant engines.
reviews.findings: The sampled merge implementation distinguishes conflict styles and incomplete-line behavior. Cargo defaults are empty; binary support is opt-in. The package excludes tests/fuzz from registry packaging and gates compatibility/replay tests behind binary.
reviews.adaptations: Acquire the pinned repository test corpus, not just a crates.io archive. Bound allocations, preserve byte paths and input bytes; handle file modes/renames/index stages separately. A conflict-free text merge is not proof of semantic correctness.
reviews.acceptance: Git differential patch/diff3 fixtures for CRLF, no terminal newline, NUL/binary data, malformed hunks, mode/rename conflicts and resource limits; enable binary-gated compatibility tests explicitly.

reviews.license: MIT OR Apache-2.0; package declaration inspected
components: cargo-about as a pinned development/release tool
reviews.reuse: Use the whole tool to produce third-party notices for each actual release composition; no need to embed it in Gitr.
reviews.findings: Accepted-license ordering chooses alternatives. Configuration can omit private or transitive crates, and manual clarifications override harvesting. Combining targets may include a dependency impossible on any single target.
reviews.adaptations: Prefer the MIT alternative when appropriate for the existing GPLv2 build; do not globally ignore private/transitive crates. Review and hash clarifications. Generate per-target/feature manifests and separately cover vendored source, fixtures, assets and native code.
reviews.acceptance: Reproducible notices for every release profile and pinned lockfile; a missing or changed license blocks release. The tool cannot establish authorship, relicensing rights or legal compatibility of a combined work.

reviews.license: MIT OR Apache-2.0; package declaration inspected
components: cargo-deny as a pinned dependency-policy tool
reviews.reuse: Use the whole tool beside cargo-about, with distinct policies for actual product compositions.
reviews.findings: Upstream documents checks for licenses, banned/duplicate dependencies, advisories and source allowlists; it explicitly disclaims legal advice. Its package excludes tests from distribution.
reviews.adaptations: No permissive blanket allowlist for all Apache/GPL/AGPL donors in the current GPLv2-only closure. Record exceptions and expiry; prohibit unreviewed Git sources and unexpected native backends. Keep licensing eligibility separate from distribution approval.
reviews.acceptance: Exercise rejected source/license/native-dependency fixtures and current locked graphs. Preserve audit database revision and offline repeatability; do not treat a green tool result as provenance proof.

reviews.license: MIT OR Apache-2.0; manifest and README inspected
reviews.reuse: Whole library candidate for optional peer asset distribution and CI artifacts, behind Gitr authorization and identity adapters.
reviews.findings: The sampled 0.104.1 manifest uses Iroh 1.0 and optional redb 4.1.0; default features include fs-store/rpc. README explicitly says this version is not production-quality and points production users to 0.35.
reviews.adaptations: Do not silently downgrade the transport or assume latest means qualified. Compare compatible release families. BLAKE3 transport hashes do not replace Git/LFS IDs; hash knowledge is not authorization. Keep storage ownership/GC, tickets, relay use and bandwidth policy explicit.
reviews.acceptance: Interrupted/corrupt range transfer, full SHA-256 reconstruction, denied cross-repository access, ticket expiry, GC races and data-retention tests; qualify the selected version on required platforms before claiming production readiness.
